text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Exports from Macedonia can only be achieved through revitalisation of large systems, says Minister for Development Abduleman Bedjeti. The government to provide $60 million from the state budget next year for development of the economy.
- Macedonian parliament ratifies several agreements regulating air transport, border and railroad traffic and protection of investments with the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.
- Defence ministry sources tell Nova Makedonija the situation in the country is stable and there are no reasons for prognoses of a new Balkan war that could start in Macedonia.

- OSCE High Commissioner for ethnic issues Max Van der Stoel says round table talks on interethnic relations in Macedonia only covered general questions and did not involve negotiations between the Macedonian government and ethnic Albanians.
- Macedonian President Kiro Gligorov to address parliament on December 24 on his presidential activities in 1996. Parliament to discuss draft 1997 state budget.

- Macedonian independent trade unions to organize peaceful demonstrations on Friday outside the government. Truck drivers and construction workers to organize blockade of streets with heavy vehicles, taxi drivers to block approaches to the city centre. Workers demanding payment of several months overdue salaries and protesting against "unjust privatisation".
